newsitem.title: INDIA: India minister says no need for coffee imports-PTI.
newsitem.headline: India minister says no need for coffee imports-PTI.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Tuesday as saying there was no need to allow coffee imports as prices have come down from recent peaks.
"There is absolutely no need for import of coffee as the prices are under control," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Ramaiah as saying in an interview in the capital New Delhi.
India, which exports most of its coffee production, has freed the coffee trade from longstanding marketing controls over the past four years. It allows free exports but does not permit imports.

In June, PTI quoted the highest-ranking civil servant in the Commerce Ministry, P.P. Prabhu, as saying the government was considering permitting coffee imports to help stabilise prices, which had risen sharply.
Domestic prices, tracking international prices, have since come down, helped by expectations of a bountiful Indian crop in 1997/98 (July-June).
Indian retail prices have stabilised at around 180 rupees per kg after soaring to 220 rupees in June from 160 in the previous month.
"No action will be taken unless it is necessary, and coffee prices have come down," PTI quoted Ramaiah as saying.
